evidence.positive: Against the shipped build (ff735801d), fired 8 concurrent first messages (4 RAS^O17 acetaminophen admins at distinct RXA-3 times + 4 ORU^R01 ABO lab results at distinct OBX-14 times) for brand-new PMRN 99510002 via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send with X-Tenant-Id mayo-mayo; all 8 ACKed AA within 46ms. App log showed 8 'Resolved patient absent from the tenant' lines (4 from MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessor, 4 from MayoHL7OruBaseProcessor) and 4 'Persisted HL7-sourced MedicationAdministration ... (wasUpdate=false)' lines, with zero 'HL7 processor ... failed' errors. DB in schema mayo-mayo: patients where pmrn=99510002 -> 1 row (SUNAND MOON, 1941-04-01, FEMALE, i.e. the RAS skeleton won the lock and the ORU threads re-read it), medication_administrations -> 4, patient_observations -> 4, hl7_inbound_messages -> 4 RAS + 4 ORU. Same result on an earlier ORU-only burst for 99510001 (1 patient, 4 observations) and on the post-restore burst for 99510004 (8/8 resolved, 1 patient, 4 admins, 4 observations, 0 errors).
evidence.negative: Two inverse checks. (1) Known-patient path must not re-enter creation: sent 1 RAS + 1 ORU (offset 7, distinct timestamps) for the now-existing 99510002; log showed the two 'Received HL7 message' lines and one new 'Persisted HL7-sourced MedicationAdministration' line but no 'Resolved patient absent' line, and DB went patients=1 (unchanged), med_admins 4->5, observations 4->5. (2) Constraint violation must not occur under the fix: grep of the full app log for 'patients_pmrn_key' returned 0 across all fixed-build bursts (before the swap and after the restore), and every inbound message's payload was stored (message counts equal stored admin/observation counts).
evidence.red_check: Compiled the parent commit's MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessor and MayoHL7OruBaseProcessor (lombok annotations replaced with an explicit logger and constructor) inside the container with javac against /app/classes:/app/libs/*, copied the resulting classes into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration/mayo/hl7 so they shadow the jar, and restarted the container (booted in 11.8s). Fired the identical 8-message burst for new PMRN 99510003: log showed exactly one pre-fix 'Created skeleton patient' line, then 7 'HL7 processor MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessor/MayoHL7OruProcessor failed for type=... tenant=mayo-mayo' errors each caused by PSQLException 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "patients_pmrn_key"' (42 matching lines, all inside this window). DB for 99510003: patients=1, medication_administrations=1, patient_observations=0, while all 8 hl7_inbound_messages rows stayed ACCEPTED, i.e. 7 of 8 messages were silently dropped exactly as the ticket describes. Reverted by deleting only the added /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration/mayo subtree (the integration dir was back to its original two Result classes), confirmed /app/libs/mayo-client-integration-0.1.101-SNAPSHOT.jar md5 unchanged (43536525a2f919a2a13afceb407a4f56 before and after), restarted, and re-ran the positive burst for 99510004: 8/8 resolved, 0 constraint errors after the restore mark.

red_check_signature: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "patients_pmrn_key"
caveats: Only the lab-result ORU subclass was exercised; the flowsheet ORU subclass shares the same MayoHL7OruBaseProcessor.process() path and was not sent separately.
The RAS cancel/completion-status path (second findOrCreatePatient call site for an unseen patient on a delete) was not exercised at runtime; only the Given administration path was.
The race was reproduced by 8 messages arriving within ~100ms on one node; cross-node contention was not simulated, but the advisory lock is database-scoped so the mechanism is the same.

Unrelated sibling race observed under the same burst on the fixed build: 4 concurrent RAS admins from the same administering provider each hit 'Key (epic_user_id)=(15573354) already exists' on the practitioners insert (hibernate WARN); all 4 admins still persisted, so no message was lost, but PractitionerService find-or-create is not serialized the way patient creation now is.
Practitioner FHIR lookup errors in the log are expected here (no Epic connectivity in this instance) and did not affect persistence.

automation.assessment: The fix commit already updated the Mockito unit tests in MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessorTest and MayoHL7OruLabResultProcessorTest to verify the processors call hl7ProcessingContext.findOrCreatePatient and never patientRepository.save directly; PatientRefreshLockPostgresConcurrencyIntegrationTest covers the lock itself. What no test locks in is the end-to-end contract this validation proved: N concurrent first messages for one PMRN through the real dispatcher and a real Postgres yield one patient row and N stored payloads. That is the assertion that would have caught the original bug and is worth one integration test; the flowsheet subclass and the RAS cancel path have no findOrCreate coverage at all.
proposed_tests: Testcontainers integration test: dispatch 4 RAS + 4 ORU messages for one unseen PMRN concurrently through HL7MessageDispatcher against Postgres; assert exactly one patients row, 4 medication_administrations, 4 patient_observations, and no DataIntegrityViolationException logged.

MayoHL7OruFlowsheetProcessorTest: unknown patient resolves via hl7ProcessingContext.findOrCreatePatient with the PID-derived skeleton and patientRepository.save is never called (mirrors the lab-result test added in the fix).

MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessorTest: completion-status-canceled message for an unseen patient captures the skeleton passed to findOrCreatePatient and asserts PID-5/7/8 mapping, not just that it was called.
Supplemental: MayoHl7PatientSkeleton.from with blank PID-5, PID-7 and PID-8 yields null name/dob/gender rather than empty strings, since all three processors now share this builder.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: Eight concurrent first RAS and ORU messages for a new Mayo PMRN produced one patient row, four stored administrations and four stored observations with no processor errors.
Negative: Follow-up messages for the now-known patient skipped patient creation and still persisted, and the PMRN unique-constraint error never appeared in the log on the fixed build.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix RAS and ORU processor classes into the running container and repeating the burst produced one skeleton and seven dropped messages with duplicate-key violations on patients_pmrn_key, and the shipped classes were restored and re-verified.

Automation: A Testcontainers concurrency test through the real dispatcher plus small unit gaps for the flowsheet and RAS cancel paths are proposed.
